title: TuPy-E: detecting hate speech in Brazilian Portuguese social media with a novel dataset and comprehensive analysis of models

bias_targets.methodology: Graph-based co-occurrence analysis of gender-specific derogatory terms (misogyny) and evaluation of fine-tuned BERTimbau models using precision, recall, and F1 scores for hierarchical hate speech classification.
Network graph analysis of terms tied to political figures and ideologies, alongside performance evaluation of BERTimbau models in classifying politically targeted hate speech.
N-gram and graph analysis of homophobic slurs, followed by evaluating BERTimbau models' classification metrics (precision, recall, F1) for detecting LGBTphobia.
Evaluating fine-tuned BERTimbau Base and Large models' precision, recall, and F1 scores in detecting racist hate speech within Brazilian Portuguese tweets.
Analyzing word frequencies related to body shaming and measuring the classification performance of BERTimbau models fine-tuned to detect body-shaming tweets.
Evaluating BERTimbau models' capabilities in classifying aporophobia (prejudice against poor people) using precision, recall, and F1 scores.
Measuring the precision, recall, and F1 scores of BERTimbau models fine-tuned to detect capacitism (ableism) in social media texts.
Evaluating the performance of BERTimbau models in identifying instances of ageism within the annotated Twitter dataset.
Evaluating fine-tuned BERTimbau models on their ability to classify religious intolerance using standard predictive metrics (precision, recall, F1).
Measuring BERTimbau models' classification metrics for detecting xenophobic hate speech targeting individuals based on geographic origin.
